newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus may complain to EC in TV row.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus may complain to EC in TV row.

text.p: Canal Plus may complain to the European Commission about an exclusive deal under which French public television channels are broadcast on a rival to its Canalsatellite digital satellite TV service, a Canal Plus spokeswoman said on Thursday.
She was confirming a report in Thursday's issue of financial daily Les Echos.
She said that Canal Plus hoped the problem would be resolved through negotiation.
However, the row so far has been waged by Canal Plus and Television Par Satellite (TPS) through submissions to Parliament, which is examining a broadcasting bill, and in the media.
Canal Plus is contesting a deal under which public channels France 2 and France 3 are broadcast exclusively by TPS, and wants to carry them on Canalsatellite.
France Television, the parent of France 2 and France 3, is a shareholder in TPS.

Top TPS officials have said Canalsatellite subscribers could get France 2 and France 3 via satellite in digital quality if Canal Plus agreed to use simulcrypt software, which would make the reception system of both services technically compatible.
Canal Plus says its subscribers should be able to receive public channels since they pay the television licence fee.
